column1: # Locations that deliberately have no row in instance/host-state.tsv. This file
# is part of the enumeration, not an escape from it: every line is a place that
# was looked at and a reason it needs no row of its own.
# prefix  a path template. `*` matches one path segment, and so does a $VAR this
#         host has no value for -- which is how one line covers per-run scratch
#         like review-dispatch.<mktemp suffix> without an edit per run.
# scope   WHICH scan the excuse applies to, and getting this wrong is how the
#           source  the drift scan only -- a path literal in tracked code that
#                   needs no row. Checked closed: tools/check-host-state.ts
#                   rejects one no tracked file names any more, so a stale
#                   excuse cannot outlive the code that justified it.
#           host    the sweep only -- something that exists on this filesystem
#                   and is not this control plane's state. A host excuse that
#                   matches nothing is REPORTED, not failed: a host getting
#                   cleaner must never turn the sweep red.
#           both    true of the literal and of the file.
# $XDG_STATE_HOME below is exactly why the column exists. It is excused as a
# source literal because meteorite/run.sh names the bare root and composes the
# real path from a variable. Letting that excuse reach the host sweep would make
# the whole of ~/.local/state invisible -- which is precisely where the
# reviewer's unlisted fixture sat when round 1 reported clean.
